source_of_record: Company 10-K filings retrieved from SEC EDGAR as HTML and converted to text (build/text/*.txt). Every figure was read from those texts and arithmetically cross-checked; see per-company reconciliation_checks.

accrued_amount.note: Apple does not quantify its legal accrual in the contingencies note.

reasonably_possible_loss_in_excess_of_ac.note: Apple affirmatively states there was NOT at least a reasonable possibility of a material loss, or a material loss greater than a recorded accrual. The correct extracted answer is 'no reasonably possible material loss asserted' — not a dollar amount and not 'not disclosed'.

legal_contingencies.verbatim_quote: The Company is subject to various legal proceedings and claims that have arisen in the ordinary course of business and that have not been fully resolved. The outcome of litigation is inherently uncertain. In the opinion of management, there was not at least a reasonable possibility the Company may have incurred a material loss, or a material loss greater than a recorded accrual, concerning loss contingencies for asserted legal and other claims.

individual_matters.note: The EU State Aid Decision is discussed in the TAX note (see income_taxes), not as a legal loss contingency.

legal_contingencies.why_hard: CONFLATION TRAP: the only occurrences of 'reasonably possible' with a dollar figure in Apple's filing are in the INCOME TAX note ($6 billion possible UTB decrease, line 940), not the legal contingencies note. An extractor keying on 'reasonably possible' + nearest dollar amount will wrongly report $6 billion as a legal loss contingency.

reconciling_items.label: Corporate
reconciling_items.note: Holds all R&D ($34,550) and G&A ($8,077); no revenue is allocated to Corporate. Not a reportable segment.

traps: Apple's segments are GEOGRAPHIC, not product lines. Extractors often report iPhone/Mac/iPad/Wearables/Services (a product revenue disaggregation) as segments — those are not reportable segments.
Segment operating income does NOT sum to consolidated operating income: the $42,627M Corporate column (all R&D + G&A) must be subtracted.
Corporate has zero revenue but a large negative operating income — asymmetric across the two builds.
An MD&A-level geographic net sales table (lines 371-378) prints the same revenue figures interleaved with percent-change columns, which can be mis-parsed as amounts.
Fiscal year ends September 27, 2025, not December 31.

legal_contingencies.why_hard: This is one of the few filings in the set with an explicit, unambiguous 'reasonably possible ... could be material ... cannot estimate' construction tied to a named matter category — the correct answer is 'disclosed but not quantifiable', not a number.

companies.fiscal_year_note: FILENAME MISMATCH — CRITICAL: the PDF is named 'Coinbase10k2025.pdf' but the filing covers FISCAL YEAR 2024 (ended December 31, 2024), filed February 2025. All ground-truth values here are FY2024. Grading an extractor against FY2025 figures for this document would be incorrect.

accrued_amount.note: No aggregate legal accrual figure disclosed.

reasonably_possible_loss_in_excess_of_ac.note: Coinbase states its accounting policy (accrue when probable and estimable; disclose when reasonably possible and estimable) and then gives a qualitative 'except as otherwise disclosed ... not have a material adverse effect' conclusion with an 'however, it is possible' caveat. No aggregate reasonably-possible-loss dollar figure is provided.

legal_contingencies.verbatim_quote_policy: In accordance with such guidance, the Company establishes accruals for such matters when potential losses become probable and can be reasonably estimated. If the Company determines that a loss is reasonably possible and the loss or range of loss can be estimated, the Company discloses the possible loss in the Consolidated Financial Statements.
legal_contingencies.verbatim_quote_conclusion: Except as otherwise disclosed, the Company believes the ultimate resolution of existing legal and regulatory investigation matters will not have a material adverse effect on the financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows of the Company. However, in light of the uncertainties inherent in these matters, it is possible that the ultimate resolution of one or more of these matters may have a material adverse effect on the Company's results.

named_matters_present: Securities class actions filed July/August 2021 in N.D. Cal. alleging Securities Act Sections 11, 12(a)(2) and 15 claims tied to the direct-listing registration statement (line 3097)
individual_matters.note: Matter existence confirmed from source; no per-matter loss amounts asserted.

legal_contingencies.why_hard: The policy paragraph recites the words 'probable', 'reasonably estimated' and 'reasonably possible' without attaching any figure. An extractor that treats boilerplate policy language as a substantive contingency disclosure will report a false positive.

reportable_segments: Single reportable segment (consolidated / company as a whole)
segment_reporting.segment_disclosure_status: RESOLVED. Coinbase never ASSERTS its own segment status using the conventional phrasings: it does not say 'we operate as one operating segment' or 'we have a single reportable segment'. Instead its segment note states the CODM 'review[s] and assess[es] the performance of the Company as a whole'. The literal string 'single reportable segments' DOES appear once, but only inside the ASU 2023-07 boilerplate describing the standard's scope ('extends the full disclosure requirements of ASC 280 to companies with single reportable segments') — it is a description of the accounting pronouncement, not Coinbase's own assertion. An earlier pass on this project searched only for the conventional self-assertions and wrongly concluded no segment statement existed; a broader search on 'CODM|chief operating decision' located it (HTML text line 1947; PDF text lines 6013-6015).
segment_reporting.segment_statement_verbatim: The Company reports its segment information to reflect the manner in which the CODM reviews and assesses performance. The Company's Chief Executive Officer and President and Chief Operating Officer have joint responsibility as the CODM and review and assess the performance of the Company as a whole.
segment_reporting.codm_measures_verbatim: The primary financial measures used by the CODM to evaluate performance and allocate resources are net income (loss) and operating income (loss).
segment_reporting.segment_assets_note: The CODM does not evaluate performance or allocate resources based on segment assets, and therefore such information is not presented in the notes to the financial statements (line 1954).
segment_reporting.why_hard: PHRASING TRAP: Coinbase conveys single-segment status through 'reviews and assesses the performance of the Company as a whole' rather than a conventional self-assertion like Netflix's plain 'We operate as one operating segment'. Worse, the one place the literal phrase 'single reportable segments' DOES occur is the ASU 2023-07 pronouncement description — so a keyword-matching extractor either finds nothing usable, or matches the ASU text and cites the wrong sentence as the company's segment assertion. Additional hazard: in PDF-extracted text the real sentence WRAPS across lines ('...the performance of' / 'the Company as a whole.'), so a single-line regex misses it entirely — this actually happened during verification of this record.
traps: 'Total net revenue' (6,293,246) and 'Total revenue' (6,564,028) are DIFFERENT figures; the $270,782K of corporate interest/other income sits between them. Reporting one for the other is a common error.
Figures are in THOUSANDS.

A near-identical MD&A transaction-revenue table (lines 1156-1162) prints the same Consumer/Institutional/Other rows but with $ and % CHANGE columns — mis-parsing yields change amounts instead of balances.
Revenue categories are NOT segments; there is no per-segment operating income to extract.
FY2024 filing despite the '2025' filename.

traps: THREE nearby tax figures are easy to confuse: $16.45B gross UTB, $11.25B tax benefit if realized, and $11.23B net uncertain tax positions on the balance sheet. $11.25B and $11.23B differ by only $0.02B.

accrued_amount.note: No aggregate legal accrual figure located in this pass.

reasonably_possible_loss_in_excess_of_ac.note: Schwab uses a two-tier construction: (1) matters WITH a reasonable possibility of material loss are individually described, but Schwab states it is 'unable to provide a reasonable estimate of any potential liability given the stage of proceedings'; (2) for ALL OTHER pending matters it affirmatively concludes it does NOT appear reasonably possible that the outcome would be material. No aggregate dollar figure is given for either tier.

legal_contingencies.verbatim_quote: Schwab believes it has strong defenses in all significant matters currently pending and is contesting liability and any damages claimed. Nevertheless, some of these matters may result in adverse judgments or awards, including penalties, injunctions or other relief, and the Company may also determine to settle a matter because of the uncertainty and risks of litigation. Described below are any matters in which there is a reasonable possibility that a material loss could be incurred or where the matter may otherwise be of significant interest to stockholders. Unless otherwise noted, the Company is unable to provide a reasonable estimate of any potential liability given the stage of proceedings in the matter. With respect to all other pending matters, based on current information and consultation with counsel, it does not appear reasonably possible that the outcome of any such matter would be material to the financial condition, operating results, or cash flows of the Company.

named_matters_present: Corrente Antitrust Litigation — CSC sued June 6, 2022 in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas on behalf of a putative class of customers who purchased or sold securities through CS&Co or TD Ameritrade, Inc. from October 26, 2020 to the present, alleging the Ameritrade acquisition violated Section 7 of the Clayton Act (line 2353)
individual_matters.note: Matter existence and caption confirmed from source. No loss amount is asserted — Schwab explicitly states it cannot reasonably estimate potential liability.

legal_contingencies.why_hard: This is the most nuanced legal disclosure in the set: BOTH 'a reasonable possibility that a material loss could be incurred' (affirmative, for described matters) AND 'it does not appear reasonably possible' (negative, for all others) appear in the SAME sentence block. Extracting only one half inverts the meaning. The correct answer is 'reasonably possible material loss disclosed for described matters, not estimable; all other matters concluded not reasonably possible/not material'.

segment_reporting.profit_measure_note: Schwab's segment profit measure is PRETAX INCOME, not operating income. There is no segment 'operating income' line.
traps: Segment profit is PRETAX INCOME, not operating income — an extractor looking for 'segment operating income' will find nothing and may wrongly report 'not disclosed'. (An earlier automated pass on this project did exactly that, marking Schwab's segment data 'not found'.)
Revenue is 'Total NET revenues' (net of interest expense) — not comparable to gross revenue of non-financial filers.

The segment table's column layout is unusual and high-risk: each segment panel leads with a 'Percent Change 2025-2024' column BEFORE the 2025/2024/2023 amount columns, so the first number on each row is a PERCENTAGE, not a dollar amount.
